title: pcell-mwall-b42 metabolism holds per individual: on fresh seed 2 a feed cut inside a disk around one cell kills that cell within 600 t while every neighbour lives on and the fed twin keeps it (2/2 targets); the global fork kills all 34 cells
summary: Fresh seed 2, the claimed world unchanged: cells form from noise (30 at t=100000; 13 persistent splits, generation 4, no merges). Global fork (world_starve.py, feed cut at t=60000): all 34 cells are gone within 600 t, while the substrate stays at a mean of 0.37. Local fork (world_local.py: the same world with the feed set to 0 only inside a disk around one cell from t=60000): for both targets (cell 23, area 358, r=14; cell 13, area 364, r=13) the target is gone by t=60588, while the 5-6 other cells within r+12 px keep their size and divide (34 -> 34-38 cells by t=70000). In the fed twin the same cell 23 is alive at t~70000 (area 354). Substrate inside the cut disk rises after the death (0.39 -> 0.73) as diffusion refills it. The cell lives mainly on the feed falling on it: the diffusive inflow, about D dS/R^2 = 3e-4, is a tenth of the local feed F(1-S) = 3.7e-3. So the cell's supply is local and individual, and the bath does not rescue it.

verdicts.limitation: Death is a threshold collapse, not exhaustion of a store: the global fork kills every cell within 600 t with bath substrate still at 0.37, and the local fork kills the target while its disk refills to 0.73. A cell has essentially no reserve; it lives on the feed flux that lands on it. One fresh seed and 2 local targets. The cut disks reach 3-4 px beyond the target wall but not into neighbours. B and H were not checked.
